issues.description: The UML diagram in problem_statement.md lists the attributes in a different order than the constructor parameter order used in the solution. The UML shows attribute order: numberOfInscribedStudents, lectureName, numberOfLecturers, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfTutors, while the solution's constructor signature uses (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). This mismatch between the UML and the implemented constructor can confuse students about the required constructor parameter order and which order to follow when implementing or instantiating Lecture objects.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended constructor parameter order explicit and consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the UML in problem_statement.md to list attributes in the same order as the intended constructor (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), or (B) change the solution (and template constructor signature example) to follow the UML order. Also update the template's constructor TODO to show the chosen parameter order so students are not uncertain which order to implement.
